S37.01.needs: a Free account with at least one notebook (or an empty account to see the empty list)
S37.01.note: The sidebar item can be hidden by the user (hideable), and the nav label also has a translation key, navProjects.
steps: Sign in and click Projects in the sidebar.
Look for the list of your notebooks, with the search box that says Search projects....
Click one notebook to open it.
Compare the list and the opened notebook with Expected.
Click Projects in the sidebar.
Click New project.
Type a name in the Project name field and click Create project.
Look for the new notebook in the list, and for the notebook page opening after creation.

S37.03.note: The save button wording was not confirmed in the code, and the Project updated toast text was seen in ProjectSettingsDialog.tsx.
steps: Create a notebook with a name and a Description, as in S37.02.
Open the notebook and click the Project options button.
Click Project settings.
Change the Name or the Description and save; look for the Project updated message and the new text.
S37.03.where: Sidebar > Projects > New project > Description, then open the notebook > Project options > Project settings

S37.04.needs: a notebook with at least one source
S37.04.note: The position of the toggle button inside the chat header was not confirmed.
steps: Open a notebook from Projects.
Click the Chats tab and open a chat.
Click the icon button whose tooltip is Project sources.
Look for the source list beside the conversation, with the Add sources button and the file list.
S37.04.where: Projects > open a notebook > Chats > open a chat > click the icon button titled Project sources

S37.06.needs: a file to upload (PDF, doc or text)
S37.06.note: The cited knowledge-files route line moved; the upload path was found through SourcesPanel handleUpload. Indexing is not visible on screen.
steps: Open a notebook and click the Sources tab.
Click Add sources, then click Upload.
Choose a PDF, doc or text file and wait for the progress to finish.
Look for the file in the source list, then ask a chat in the notebook about it and compare with Expected.
S37.06.where: Projects > open a notebook > Sources > Add sources > Upload

S37.10.needs: an outside account (Google) with Drive files
S37.10.note: Unfinished: the picker needs GOOGLE_PICKER_API_KEY and GOOGLE_PICKER_APP_ID. Without them the tile may show Coming soon or the error Adding files from Google Drive is not available yet.
steps: Open a notebook and click the Sources tab.
Click Add sources, then click Google Drive.
Pick files in the Google picker window and confirm.
Look for the picked files in the source list.
S37.10.where: Projects > open a notebook > Sources > Add sources > Google Drive

S37.11.note: The cited route line moved. The Sources tab also has a separate Notes section (ProjectNotes.tsx), not checked as a source route.
steps: Open a notebook, click the Sources tab, click Add sources.
Click Text input.
Type a title in the field with the placeholder e.g. Project notes, and paste or type text in the box.
Save it as a source and look for the new text source in the list.
S37.11.where: Projects > open a notebook > Sources > Add sources > Text input

steps: Open a notebook and open the Chats tab.
Start a chat and type a question that the sources can answer.
Read the answer and look for source names or citation chips under it.
Compare the answer with the sources in the notebook.
Open the notebook and click the Project options button.
Click Project settings.
Type a rule in the Instructions box, for example Respond in Spanish, and save.
Start a new chat in the notebook, ask a question, and check that the reply follows the rule.
S37.15.where: Projects > open a notebook > Project options > Project settings > Instructions

S37.19.note: The code does not show the chip is a button; the preview opens from the knowledgeFile and page link. Click behaviour was not confirmed.
steps: Open a notebook and ask a question in a chat that the sources answer.
Look under the answer for a source chip with the file name and page.
Click the chip.
Check that the source preview opens at the cited page.
S37.19.where: Projects > open a notebook > Chats > ask a question > click the source chip under the answer

labels.text: Everyone in the workspace can view

S37.34.needs: a team workspace and a second account in the same workspace
S37.34.note: The audit marks the UI as unfinished. Outside a team workspace the dialog says Only you can open this project.
steps: Open the notebook and click the Project options button.
Click Share. The dialog title is Share followed by the notebook name.
Choose Everyone in the workspace can view, or set a member to Can view or Can edit.
Sign in as the other account and check that it can open the notebook with that access.
S37.34.where: Projects > open a notebook > Project options > Share

S37.37.note: The audit marks the UI as unfinished. No separate bring-context control was found; the project picker is the handoff.
steps: In the main chat, click the Project button in the composer bar.
Pick a notebook from the list.
Send a question that needs the notebook sources.
Check that the answer uses the notebook sources.
S37.37.where: Main chat > composer bar Project button > pick a notebook

S37.38.needs: a second app signed in with the same account
S37.38.note: Sync is server-side; no control was found in the code, and the other apps were not checked.
steps: Sign in with the same account in another app (desktop, mobile or the Chrome extension).
Open Projects in that app.
Check that the same notebook list appears and that the notebook opens with its sources.
S37.38.where: Projects list in another app signed in with the same account
